{"id": "411700fd-f4e6-4822-8d6c-7c0d738dd889", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The timeout is almost certainly caused by the security group. It has no inbound rule that allows SSH (TCP 22) from your IP.

You didn't say which instance, so I checked all three running Linux instances. They share the same subnet and security group, so the finding applies to each of them.

**Instances checked**
- i-1234567890abcdef0_1 (203.0.113.10)
- i-1234567890abcdef0_2 (203.0.113.11)
- i-1234567890abcdef0_3 (203.0.113.12)

All three are named "ssm-skill-test", are t3.nano, and sit in subnet-4fe1f806 in vpc-7ffc8619.

**What I found**
- **Security group (sg-a8544cd4, "default"):** The only inbound rule allows all traffic from members of the same security group. Nothing allows port 22 from the internet or from your IP, so SSH packets are dropped and the connection times out. This is the root cause.
- **Instance health:** The system and instance status checks are both `ok` on all three, so the instances are up and not hung.
- **Public IP:** All three have a public IPv4 address.
- **Routing:** The VPC's main route table has an active `0.0.0.0/0` route to the internet gateway igw-ea7c458d.
- **Network ACL:** The default ACL allows all inbound and outbound traffic.
- **Key pair:** None of the three instances has a key pair, so key-based SSH wouldn't work even once the port is open. These look like they're meant to be reached through SSM Session Manager. If that's your normal access method, SSH timing out is expected.

**Fix, depending on how you connect**
1. **Via SSH:** Add an inbound rule to sg-a8544cd4 for TCP 22 from your own IP (`x.x.x.x/32`), not `0.0.0.0/0`. You'll also need a key pair or another login method on the instance. A key pair can't be added to a running instance, so that means EC2 Instance Connect or a new or re-keyed instance.
2. **Via SSM Session Manager:** This needs no inbound port. It does need the SSM agent, an instance profile with SSM permissions, and outbound HTTPS access, and I can verify those if you want.

I can add the SSH rule to the security group. It needs your approval, and I'd need your source IP or CIDR. Note that sg-a8544cd4 is the VPC's default group, so the rule would apply to every instance that uses it. If you meant a different instance than these three, tell me the ID or name and I'll check it.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
